title: Singer-Hieronymus: Fort Ancient Villages in Scott County
summary: In Scott County, Fort Ancient farmers built a chain of circular villages at the Singer-Hieronymus site between about A.D. 1200 and 1550.
bodyMarkdown:
In Scott County, Fort Ancient farmers built a chain of circular villages between about A.D. 1200 and 1550. UK archaeologists mapped Singer Village in the late 1990s, then found more rings on the adjoining Hieronymus farm; later geophysics pushed the count to at least six or seven midden stains—concentric house, burial, and trash zones around open plazas, with corn-beans-squash agriculture and two low burial mounds on the largest circle.

The complex looks like one community shifting over generations, a rare Kentucky window on how Fort Ancient towns moved without leaving the same small area.
Source: [https://archaeology.ky.gov/Find-a-Site/Pages/Singer-Hieronymus.aspx](https://archaeology.ky.gov/Find-a-Site/Pages/Singer-Hieronymus.aspx)
